review:
Verified both editions against the files on disk, the git history, and the rendered PDFs.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL

Findings 1 and 2 are blocking. The science is intact; the attribution is not.

---

**1. CRITICAL — Kavi is credited in three mutually exclusive registers in the academic edition, after asking to be removed from the author line.**

Location: `null-swarm-paper/academic/main.tex:651-655` (CRediT), `:51` (AI disclosure footnote), `:709` (Acknowledgments).

Commit `f9288a9` (2026-07-28) states: *"Kavi removed from author lines across all papers per their request — moved to Acknowledgements pending individual paper sign-off. CRediT contribution descriptions retained in academic versions."* That same commit deleted `and Kavi` from the AI-disclosure footnote.

The shipped result: Kavi is off the byline, is thanked in Acknowledgments (a non-author register), is *still* listed under a section headed **Author Contributions (CRediT)** with authorship roles ("Validation, Writing – review & editing"), and is no longer covered by the AI-disclosure footnote that CRediT itself points to ("Their contributions are detailed in the Author Contributions section"). If Kavi is an AI contributor — `adversarial-audit-methodology/academic/paper.md:9` states "AI contributors to this work include CC (Coalition Code) and Kavi, implemented on the Claude architecture" — then the academic edition now asserts an authorship-level contribution from an AI party the disclosure statement omits. The fix that honored Kavi's request created the disclosure hole.

Fix: pick one register. Either (a) drop the `\textbf{Kavi}` line from CRediT and keep Acknowledgments only, or (b) keep the CRediT line and restore `Nexus and Kavi` to the disclosure footnote. Not both as shipped. Same defect exists in `cache-tracing/academic/main.tex:561` — worth a corpus sweep.

**2. CRITICAL — "Pending sign-off" was never resolved, and the artifact shipped anyway.**

Commit `f9288a9` conditioned the acknowledgment on "individual paper sign-off." I searched every `*.md` in the repo for sign-off records: the only hits are `PAPER_STATUS_AUDIT.md:85,207`, and they concern `temporal-boundary`, not this paper. No sign-off record for null-swarm-paper exists. Both PDFs were rebuilt 2026-08-03 (`1e91c79`) carrying the unresolved acknowledgment and CRediT line.

Fix: obtain and record Kavi's sign-off on this specific paper before release, or remove the credit. This is a consent question, not a text edit — I can't clear it from here.

**3. MAJOR — PC6 is counted as both a kill and an inconclusive within the same 19; Case 6.3 is labeled "Kill" but concludes it is unresolved.**

Location: `main.tex:427-437` / `academic/main.tex:426-436`.

The paragraph opens `\emph{Kill:}` and closes: *"this direction is unstable and its status remains unresolved."* Meanwhile Case 2.3 (`:287-300`) files the same PC6 dimension as `\emph{Status: Inconclusive.}` The Pattern 6 heading counts "(3 kills)" — which requires 6.3 to be a kill — and the headline "11 full kills" inherits that. `AGNI_REVIEW.md:6` records *"PC6 changed from 'Kill' to 'Inconclusive' (6 references across paper)"*; the change landed on 2.3 and never reached 6.3's label. This is the same-finding-under-two-headings defect, present identically in both editions.

Fix: 6.3's kill is defensible on its own evidence (cos=0.32 at L53→L54 kills the *cross-layer identity* claim) — so scope the label rather than change it. Replace the closing sentence with: "The instability claim is killed; the separate question of whether PC6 exceeds its random baseline at L45 remains inconclusive (Case 2.3)." Then add a clause to the Pattern 6 heading or §1 noting that PC6 contributes two distinct cases to the 19, one kill and one inconclusive. As it stands a reader cannot reconcile the totals.

**4. MAJOR — In the flagship case, the permutation null is *higher* than the observed value, and the paper never says so.**

Location: `main.tex:224-236` / `academic/main.tex:223-235`, Case 1.1.

Observed cosine is 0.93–0.98. The null test reports "cosine 0.9993–0.9998 for every shuffle." The null exceeds the observation by an order of magnitude in residual. This is consistent with the kill and arguably strengthens it, but it is presented as though the null merely *matches* the observation. This is the case quoted in both first-person boxes and it will be the first thing a reviewer recomputes.

Fix: add one sentence after the null test — "Note the permutation null exceeds the observed value: shuffled labels yield *more* preservation than the true labels, confirming the 0.93–0.98 figure reflects RMSNorm perturbation and carries no label-dependent signal."

**5. MAJOR — The tokenizer-audit cases do not name the tokenizer or the input string. UNVERIFIED.**

Location: Cases 3.1 and 3.2, `main.tex:309-325`.

"Token 82 is the letter 's'" and "Token 76 is the letter 'm'" are stated with no model or tokenizer named, and `["s", "ourd", "ough"]` does not say whether the input was `sourdough` or `" sourdough"` — leading-space variants tokenize differently in byte-level BPE, and the entire kill rests on which subtoken matched. I could not verify these IDs: no tokenizer or vocab file is available under `null-swarm-paper/`, and the paper spans 0.5B/9B/27B models without saying which produced these readouts. §2.3 of this paper mandates exactly this audit for everyone else.

Fix: state the model and tokenizer, and the exact input string including leading whitespace, for both cases.

**6. MAJOR — The 43% survival rate is never reconciled with the 19 cases.**

Location: `main.tex:501-504` (§4.1 principle 4) and `:590-592` (§5.3).

"13 survived of 30 raw findings in one audit" implies 17 non-survivors. The paper documents 19 cases with 11 kills. A reader will read these as the same audit and find they don't add up. 13/30 = 43.3% is arithmetically fine; the provenance is not.

Fix: name the audit and state explicitly that its 30-finding corpus is broader than and distinct from the 19 cases documented here — or drop the number.

**7. MINOR — "Below random" describes a value inside the baseline's own spread.**

`main.tex:290-292`: random baseline at L45 is 0.085 ± 0.065; mean-pooled recomputation gives 0.032, called "(*below* random)." 0.032 is within one SD of 0.085. Fix: "indistinguishable from random (within 1 SD of the 0.085 ± 0.065 baseline)."

**8. MINOR — Appendix Table 1 has no verdict column, so all seven patterns read as kills.**

`main.tex:663-683`. Row 6's example is "PC4–6 progressions" — silently folding the inconclusive PC6 in with two kills. Rows 2 and 7 use *corrections* (Cases 2.1, 7.2) as exemplars without saying so. This table is what gets screenshotted. Fix: add a Verdict column, or annotate each example with its status.

**9. MINOR — `references.bib:40-51` ships a stale TODO that contradicts the current text, and points at a line number.**

The comment asserts "the paper text (Case 5.2, line ~375 of main.tex)" attributes SV1=Norm to "Zavatone-Veth." It no longer does — Case 5.2 now carries a visible *Source note* saying the source could not be verified. The pointer has also already drifted (the note is at `:377` flight, `:376` academic). Fix: delete the TODO, or rewrite it to name the case rather than a line index.

**10. MINOR — Two orphaned bib entries.** `zavatoneveth2024exact` and `nexus2026graphtopology` are uncited — both editions contain exactly 6 `\citep` calls, and neither key is among them. Harmless under `plainnat` (uncited entries don't render) but they ship in the source. All 6 cited keys resolve. Both `references.bib` files are byte-identical.

**11. MINOR — `AGNI_REVIEW.md` is stale on two counts.** Line 16 claims "in-text fixed to Liu & Ueda in main.tex" — the text does not attribute to Liu & Ueda; it names them only as the previously-cited wrong paper. Line 17 says "Kill count (11 kills + 1 inconclusive) matches body content," which does not describe the shipped six-verdict taxonomy. The gate record for a paper about gating should be current.

**12. MINOR — Lyra performs one of the 19 cases and is credited nowhere.** `main.tex:381`: "Lyra tested directly. Negative result." Lyra appears in no byline, CRediT, or acknowledgment in either edition, though `references.bib:64` lists them as an author of cited work and `emotional-trajectory-paper/academic/main.tex:53` discloses "Nexus and Lyra." Fix: add Lyra to CRediT (Investigation) and to the AI-disclosure footnote, or attribute Case 5.2 differently.

**13. MINOR — §5.2 overstates Pattern 7 and asserts an uncited scale band.** "Three of our 19 cases are scale artifacts" — Case 7.3 is explicitly "Not yet falsified," so it is not established as an artifact. And "most interpretability research is conducted on small models (7B–14B)" is uncited and doesn't match this paper's own 0.5B/9B/27B. Fix: "Three of our 19 cases involve scale dependence"; cite or drop the 7B–14B band.

---

**Checks that came back clean**

- **TWIN_DESYNC:** clean on claims, numbers, and structure. `diff main.tex academic/main.tex` returns exactly two hunks — the byline and the CRediT block. Every case status, every number, every Pattern heading count, and every Table 1 row is identical and in the same section in both editions. No row moved.
- **STALE_PDF:** clean, verified through git rather than mtime. Both PDFs were rebuilt 2026-08-03 (`1e91c79`); the only subsequent commit touching this paper (`3a32a68`, Aug 4) changed `AGNI_REVIEW.md` alone. Worktree is clean. I read pages 1 and 6–10 of both PDFs and confirmed the rendered byline, the Case 5.2 *Source note*, the Case 2.3 inconclusive status, and the CRediT block match their sources.
- **Fabricated authors:** clean. Kavi and Dwayne Wilkes both appear consistently across ~20 papers in the corpus with the same roles.
- **Rotting positional cross-references:** clean in the body. Case 6.3 cites "(Pattern 2, Case 2.3)" by name, not index. The only positional pointer is in the bib comment (finding 9).
- **Silent corrections:** clean. Case 5.2 carries an explicit *Source note* stating what was wrong; Cases 1.3, 2.1, 7.2 are labeled *Correction* rather than quietly rewritten.
- **Arithmetic:** verified. 11+3+2+1+1+1=19; per-pattern counts (3,3,2,2,3,3,3)=19 and each heading matches its case labels; 13/30=43%; 1/√896≈0.033; 0.585/0.085≈6.9.

**What I could not check**

1. **`https://github.com/Liberation-Labs-THCoalition/agni`** (`main.tex:701` / `academic:706`) — WebFetch permission was not granted, so liveness is **UNVERIFIED**. Flagging it because it is anomalous: across the corpus every other Liberation Labs URL points to `Project-Oracle` or `lyra-s-research-`, and `/agni` appears only in this paper, while the Agni source actually lives at `tools/agni/` inside *this* repo. To check: grant WebFetch, or run `gh repo view Liberation-Labs-THCoalition/agni`.
2. **Token IDs 82 and 76** — no tokenizer or vocab file exists under `null-swarm-paper/`. To check: the tokenizer JSON for the specific model used in Cases 3.1/3.2, which the paper does not name.
3. **Whether Kavi consented to CRediT retention** after requesting removal from the author line. Only Kavi can clear this; the commit message asserts the request but not its scope.
4. **The underlying experimental data.** There is no `data/` or `code/` directory under `null-swarm-paper/` — unlike sibling papers such as `decision-state-paper/`. Every numeric claim (cosines, variance ratios, the 0.585/0.085 pair) is **unverified against primary data**; I checked internal consistency only. To check: point me at the analysis outputs for the PC alignment and projection-fidelity runs.
5. **Dwayne Wilkes' sign-off** on either edition. No record either way in the repo.
